text: {"statement":"A calm Caribbean resort garden extends the villa’s limestone plinth into a generous, veranda-centred pool court. A close, level limestone terrace keeps the water visually connected to shaded dining and a separate garden lounge, while four loungers face the turquoise pool. A north limestone arrival approach is framed as a disciplined palm avenue, then opens to garden panels and a composed south pool lawn. Ten medium palms are deliberately grouped between the paired arrival rhythm, pool-side grove and planted edges; layered tropical boundary bands give privacy, shade and depth without closing the broad garden. Restrained bollards support arrival and garden circulation as discreet daylight details.","pool":{"scale":"generous","alignment":"veranda-centre","separation":"close","water":"turquoise"},"terrace":{"finish":"limestone","sunbeds":"four","social":"dining-and-lounge"},"arrival":{"boundary":"north","finish":"limestone","character":"palm-avenue"},"planting":{"palms":"ten","stature":"medium","beds":"layered-tropical","lawn":"garden-panels"},"lighting":"arrival-and-garden","intentions":["Keep the veranda as the principal shaded dining threshold, with pool water and limestone terrace reading as one continuous outdoor room.","Use paired palms to make the north arrival legible, then release the approach into the open forecourt rather than a densely planted entrance.","Group the remaining palms as a south garden grove and boundary accents; avoid isolated palms or an even perimeter rhythm.","Build four layered tropical boundary bands for privacy and cooling shade, preserving clear central lawn panels and long pool views.","Place the garden lounge slightly apart from dining so relaxed conversation does not compete with veranda meals.","Use modest bollards only to clarify arrival and garden movement; they are decorative landscape details, not a night-lighting scheme."]}
